question: What is the difference between .a .b and .a.b?
shortAnswer: Descendant combinator vs AND on the same element.
detailedAnswer: .a .b matches .b inside .a. .a.b matches an element with both classes.

question: Explain child, sibling, and adjacent sibling combinators.
detailedAnswer: They don't select ancestors. Whitespace descendant is more expensive/broad than >.

question: When do you use :is() vs :where()?
shortAnswer: Both list selectors; :is() keeps specificity of its most specific arg; :where() is always zero.
detailedAnswer: :where() is great for resets. :is() for grouping without repetition.

question: What does :has() enable?
shortAnswer: Parent/ancestor selection based on descendants — previously impossible in CSS.
detailedAnswer: Powerful but can be style-invalidating costly. Use thoughtfully for UI states.

question: Attribute selectors — equals vs contains vs prefix?
shortAnswer: [attr=val], *= contains, ^= prefix, $= suffix, ~= word, |= hyphen code.
detailedAnswer: Useful for language, data attributes, partial href matches. Prefer exact when possible.

question: Pseudo-classes vs pseudo-elements?
shortAnswer: Pseudo-classes select states (:hover, :focus-visible); pseudo-elements style fragments (::before, ::marker).
detailedAnswer: Single vs double colon historically mixed; use :: for modern pseudo-elements.

question: Why prefer :focus-visible over :focus for outlines?
shortAnswer: Shows focus ring mainly for keyboard users, reducing mouse-focus noise.
detailedAnswer: Don't remove outlines without :focus-visible replacement. Accessibility requirement.

question: How do specificity traps happen with IDs in selectors?
shortAnswer: IDs outweigh many classes, making overrides painful.
detailedAnswer: Avoid IDs in CSS hooks; use classes/data attributes. Prefer layers over escalating specificity.

question: What are structural pseudo-classes like nth-child useful for?
shortAnswer: Selecting by position without extra classes — zebra rows, first/last, formulas.
detailedAnswer: nth-child counts all children; nth-of-type filters by type. Off-by-one common.

question: Selector performance myths — what matters today?
shortAnswer: Extremely deep selectors rarely dominate; invalidations and layout do. Still keep selectors intentional.
detailedAnswer: Avoid universal+expensive patterns in hot paths. Measure before micro-optimizing selectors.

question: How do you style a form control only when invalid after interaction?
shortAnswer: :user-invalid / :user-valid (and older patterns with classes) avoid showing errors too early.
detailedAnswer: Pair with a11y messaging. Don't rely on color alone.

question: Explain :not() limitations and nesting.
shortAnswer: :not() can take complex selectors in modern CSS; specificity depends on arguments.
detailedAnswer: Overuse reduces readability. Combine with :is for grouping.

question: Establish selector conventions for a large codebase.
shortAnswer: Forbid IDs, prefer data-testid only for tests, document :has usage, lint complexity, BEM or utilities.
detailedAnswer: Consistency beats cleverness. Codemod migrations when conventions change.
